articles.title: Elon Musk looks to break up with MAGA. To what end?
articles.summary: Elon Musk has certainly seemed to embrace the Make America Great Again movement. Why does that matter? Because the Tesla and Space X CEO now appears to be distancing himself.

image.caption: Elon Musk listens as Donald Trump speaks at a campaign event on Oct. 5, 2024, in Butler, Pa. Since spending a record amount of money on losing candidates during this month's midterms, the world's richest man has said he is 'not MAGA.' (Alex Brandon/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
Elon Musk has certainly seemed to embrace the Make America Great Again movement. Why does that matter? Because the Tesla and Space X CEO now appears to be distancing himself.
'I'm not MAGA', Musk said this week, 2 years after declaring himself 'dark MAGA'

From his first time donning a black MAGA hat and declaring himself "dark MAGA" at an October 2024 rally for Donald Trump to his multimillon-dollar splurge on Republican candidates ahead of this month's midterms, Elon Musk has certainly seemed to embrace the Make America Great Again movement.
Why does that matter? Because the Tesla and Space X CEO now appears to be distancing himself from his MAGA bonafides, saying that he never really considered himself a MAGA adherent.
"I'm not MAGA," Musk declared earlier this week, in an interview with The New York Times.

"I'm not sure what MAGA means," he said during the newspaper's DealBook Summit. "If that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don't have that. I think there are positives and negatives in both parties."
That may come as a surprise considering Musk made at least five appearances between 2024 and 2025 in which he associated himself with the movement, according to Mediaite, a news website.

items: Elon Musk gets little bang for his buck in U.S. midterms, with possible Democratic investigations to come

blocks.text: But Musk's MAGA split appears to come at a time when association to the brand could prove to be a business and legal liability for the world's richest man.
"It's so transparently convenient," said Matthew Dallek, a professor of political management and historian at the D.C.-based George Washington University, who has researched the MAGA movement.
Musk's comments follow the Republicans' disastrous showing in the U.S. midterms and the so-called Democratic blue wave that saw the party take control of the House and the Senate.
Along with MAGA-boosting appearances, Musk also spent more than $400 million U.S. on Trump-aligned Republican candidates in the midterms — the most money of any individual campaign donor.
Can Musk disassociate from MAGA?
"Now that [MAGA]'s on the losing side, all of a sudden, he's not MAGA," said Todd Belt, a professor of political management at George Washington University.
"I mean, come on. This is just laughable. This is the guy who glossed himself 'dark MAGA' and had black MAGA stuff put together ... when Trump took over. He was completely in with it."
Prof. Matthew Dallek says Elon Musk, seen speaking before Donald Trump at a campaign rally on Oct. 27, 2024, made his 'MAGA bed' and now must lie in it. (Evan Vuccu/The Associated Press)
Dallek said Musk has spent years making his "MAGA bed."
"Now he's got to lie in it, even when it's politically uncomfortable."

Musk, who also urged his followers on X to vote Republican, now says he feels "pretty foolish" for spending so much money on the midterms. He also said in his NYT interview that ideologically he is "quite moderate" and doesn't have any "extreme political views."
But Dallek said if he's really such a moderate and not part of the MAGA ranks, there were non-MAGA Republicans he could have backed during the elections.
Instead, Musk spent around $200 million US backing Texas Senate nominee Ken Paxton, who Dallek called, "arguably the most MAGA of all the midterm candidates."

items: Elon Musk calls documentary about him a 'hit piece' after buzzy debut
Satellite limitations imposed by Musk's SpaceX pose danger for Ukraine, Zelenskyy says

blocks.text: Musk has based himself and several of his companies in Texas, including Tesla, SpaceX ‌and a planned chipmaking venture between the two. But the state is almost all blue following the U.S. midterms.
"The government is no longer in the hands of his allies," Dallek said. "He is in a very vulnerable position. Businesses are very vulnerable."

Dallek also questioned just how "moderate" Musk is, as he's has turned X into a platform for extremist views. As well, a February 2025 NBC News report said Musk had been encouraging right-wing political movements, policies and administrations in at least 18 countries as part of a global push to slash immigration and curtail regulation of business.
"It's just transparently false when he says, 'I'm a moderate,'" Dallek said.
What's driving Musk's MAGA retreat?
One reason: The MAGA brand is at its lowest net favourability ever, said CNN’s chief data analyst Harry Enten.
"It is a brand that is failing amongst the American public," he said.
But perhaps more importantly, Musk may be trying to engender better relations with Democrats as he faces government probes and red tape.
Alex Gibney warns of Elon Musk's 'unchecked power' in new documentary
Democrats have indicated they may want to investigate the months Musk spent in 2025 spearheading the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).
DOGE team activities led to widespread dismantling of foreign aid programs, as well as allegations that team members breached privacy laws by illegally accessing the sensitive data of Americans.
Musk may also face slower approvals for the billions of dollars Space X plans to invest in data centre campuses in Texas and Arizona.

"They're going to be turning their eyes toward him and his space facilities, and the environmental issues that they're causing and tax issues," Belt said. "Things that could really make life difficult for him. He doesn't want to poke the bear."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Mark Gollom is a Toronto-based reporter with CBC News. He covers Canadian and U.S. politics and current affairs.
With files from The Associated Press and Reuters

articles.title: How Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost most of his belongings to auction after filming the show
articles.summary: Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost many of his personal belongings earlier this year, including a painting of a "cheetah dressed as a general," his PlayStation 5 and many household…

image.caption: Daniel Kilby, seen at left in a screenshot from his stint on Survivor, returned to Canada to find all of his stuff was being put up for auction because he missed a few of his payments for a storage locker he'd been using. (Robert Voets/CBS)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost many of his personal belongings earlier this year, including a painting of a "cheetah dressed as a general," his PlayStation 5 and many household appliances, after missed payments on a storage locker while he was on the show led to his belongings being put up for auction.
Kilby says a 'dumb mistake' led to about $2,000 worth of stuff in a locker going to the highest bidder

Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost many of his personal belongings earlier this year, including a painting of a "cheetah dressed as a general," his PlayStation 5 and many household appliances, after missed payments on a storage locker while he was on the show led to them being put up for auction.
"That's where it's been annoying … I'm like, 'Oh, I want to make a sparkling water. JK, you can't,'" said the 30-year-old game designer who now lives in Halifax.

Kilby, who'd been living in London, Ont., was renting at the time, and his lease was coming up. He didn't want to pay rent while filming the 51st season of the hit reality competition, so he stored most of his belongings in a storage locker for what he says was around $100 a month and moved in with his girlfriend in Florida.
There, he could begin his Survivor training, including learning to swim and practicing fire-making.
But on his flight to Florida in February, he says he lost his wallet. So he had to get a new debit card and update his payments. The problem? There was one payment he forgot to update.

He says he realized in mid-April — the weekend before he left to film in Fiji — that he hadn't updated his payment info with the StorageMart in London. He says he tried to call the location but couldn't update his details with the person he spoke to, and he ultimately decided to leave it until after the show was filmed.
Kilby stands next to one of his prized possessions, his 'cheetah dressed as a general' painting. (Submitted by Daniel Kilby)
At the time, he says he was more focused on living his dream and getting a shot at a million dollars on Survivor.
"I also, like, low-key did not expect them to actually auction my stuff. I thought this was like a dumb mistake that I'd have to pay when I got back," said Kilby.
Arriving home
Kilby placed 11th on the season and was voted out on the eighth episode, which aired on Nov. 11. So no million-dollar prize. Instead, he returned in June to find a very different financial matter.
The first email he read upon returning to Canada was that his storage locker — and all his stuff — was going up for auction.

While he'd been away, StorageMart had tried to contact him to update his payment information and inform him he had missed at least three payments. But since he was stuck on an island at the time with no connection to the outside world, they were unable to reach him.
"My phone is blown up. I have like a hundred emails from them being like, 'Hey, you haven't paid,'" said Kilby.

items: 'What just happened?' Jeff Probst spoils Survivor 50 finale result live on air
Survivor changed reality TV. Now it’s celebrating its 50th season

blocks.text: Kilby reached out to the storage unit company, hoping he could get his stuff back. He says he was told he would need to cough up $2,000 and retrieve his stuff immediately to do so. It was a lot of money, plus he'd need to rent a vehicle that could hold it all.
"Plus, I'm like, a lot of my stuff sucked," said Kilby, who estimates it was probably worth about $2,000 altogether.
CBC reached out to StorageMart for information on its policies around late payments and when a unit goes up for auction but didn't receive a response before publication.

StorageMart's website says there is no grace period for late payments, and that late fees will apply if payments are late, with the specifics dictated on a customer's lease. StorageMart also has an online payment portal for customers, as well as a helpline it says is operated 24/7.
Kilby came in 11th on the latest season of Survivor, which is still airing. (Robert Voets/CBS)
So he had another idea. Now that his stuff was up for auction, he could just bid on it and hope no one else was too interested.

With his bid sitting around $400, he was feeling good that he would be reunited with his belongings. But at the last second, someone with the username "Prince C" made a bid and won the auction for $441.
"It's brutal; it's sad," said Kilby. "I thought we were just winning it, so I felt kind of dumb there. But I also felt kind of relieved because I'm like, 'OK, I don't have to go pick it up.'"
'It's a funny story'
Kilby said the possessions in the locker ranged from IKEA furniture to his collection of Pokemon cards.

He tried scouring Facebook Marketplace in London after the locker sold, hoping he would see some of his stuff pop up. He even posted on Reddit, hoping someone could point him to the buyer. There are some personal belongings he wishes he could get back.

"There's, like, some sentimental thing. So I had this, like, weird painting of a cheetah dressed as a general. I thought that was really cool," said Kilby. "My mom knit a bear that's in there. That sucks."
Plus there are all the household appliances such as a SodaStream and a blender that he's needed to replace.
The rest of the stuff? He's OK to live without. Since filming the show, Kilby and his girlfriend moved to Halifax, and he says many of the items in that locker wouldn't have made the trip.
"It's a funny story, and I'm somebody who lives my life trying to do things in a way that you get a funny story at the end," said Kilby.
"It's like, hey, the passion for Survivor made me just completely [lose my stuff]."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Philip Drost is a network senior writer for CBC News based in Fredericton. You can reach him at philip.drost@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Quebec's popular PEQ program is closed — again. People counting on it want answers
articles.summary: The popular immigration pathway known as the PEQ was temporarily revived earlier this year. The first period for applications was open between July 2 and Oct. 31, and it's not clear when the Quebec…

image.caption: This protest took place on Nov. 17, 2025, in Montreal as people gathered to denounce the plan to scrap the Programme de l'expérience québécoise, also known as the PEQ program. (Samir Bendjafer/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Montreal·New

The popular immigration pathway known as the PEQ was temporarily revived earlier this year. The first period for applications was open between July 2 and Oct. 31, and it's not clear when the Quebec government will open a second window for applicants.
PEQ was revived this year with 1st application window open from July 2 to Oct. 31
Three weeks after the Quebec government ended the first phase of applications for a popular immigration pathway program, there’s no word on when the second will begin.
And for many people hoping to solidify their future in the province, the clock is ticking.
"Their future is at stake," said Sabrina Kouider-Philippon, the vice-president of group called Le Quebec c'est nous aussi, which loosely translates to "We are also part of Quebec."
"Federal work permits are expiring, work permits aren't getting renewed so these people are losing their statuses and their ability to work and support their families."
For years, the Quebec Experience Program, also known as the PEQ, was a fast track to permanent residency.

The former Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ) government scrapped it in November 2025 and replaced it with a new program known as the PSTQ, which has been criticized as a more restricted pathway toward permanent residency.

items: Quebec temporarily revives PEQ immigration pathway, but advocates call it an 'insult'

blocks.text: After much public outcry, the CAQ temporarily revived the PEQ earlier this year with plans to shut it down for good in 2028. A first window for applications opened this year between July 2 and Oct. 31.
“It is therefore no longer possible to present an application through this program,” reads a message on the Quebec government’s website.
“There has been no decision regarding a new period to accept applications.”

Sabrina Kouider-Philippon, a spokesperson for the group Le Quebec c'est nous aussi, says the lack of clarity surrounding the PEQ program takes a mental toll on people hoping to build their lives in the province. (Guillaume Renaud/CBC)
The second window could open any time between now and July 2028. That lack of clarity is unacceptable, according to Kouider-Philippon.
"People can't make any plans for the future with so much uncertainty."
PQ now in charge

What happens next with the PEQ is largely up to the Parti Québécois (PQ) — the sovereignist party that promised the lowest annual limit for permanent immigration out of the five major parties during the election campaign.
The PQ promised to lower the annual limit from 45,000 to 35,000.

items: What's changing in Quebec’s immigration system — and why it's sparking backlash

blocks.text: In a statement, the spokesperson for Quebec's new Immigration Minister Catherine Gentilcore, said the government is committed to offering a "predictable path toward permanent residence to people who fit criteria established by Quebec," referring to French-language skills and their fit in the province's job market.

"The handling of the PEQ has to also take into consideration our ability to take in people and objectives the province has set for immigration, integration and francization," wrote spokesperson Éli Dubois.
A spokesperson for Quebec's immigration minister says there is no planned date for the reopening of the PEQ program after it closed on Oct. 31. (Ivanoh Demers/Radio-Canada)
Ottawa also needs to step up, group says
The spokesperson for Quebec's immigration minister reiterated that there is no planned date to reopen the PEQ program at the moment.
"The reopening of the program this past summer generated a high volume of requests in a short period of time," he wrote.
He said the PQ government's overall immigration plan will be presented before the holidays.
CBC News asked the province's Immigration Ministry how many PEQ applications it received between July 2 and Oct. 31. We're waiting to hear back.
Kouider-Philippon's group is also asking Ottawa to extend work permits for those caught in limbo while the PEQ program is on hold.
Catherine Gentilcore, who became an MNA after winning a byelection in Terrebonne in 2025, is the province's immigration minister under the Parti Québécois government. (Sylvain Roy Roussel/CBC)

In a statement, a spokesperson for Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) said it's working closely with Quebec "to support the province's labour market needs and to facilitate pathways" to permanent residence.

The IRCC spokesperson highlighted measures put in place both by Quebec or Ottawa to prioritize people with expiring work permits for permanent immigration selection as well as provide or extend work permits to people on the verge of being selected.
The work permit measure, however, seems to apply to the PSTQ program.
Quebec’s PEQ program to return temporarily
The battle continues
For Le Quebec c'est nous aussi, reopening the PEQ for a second wave of applications is just the beginning.

The group believes the program should reopen permanently and for anyone who was in Quebec before Nov. 19, 2025 — the end of the PEQ program before the CAQ revived it — should have an opportunity to apply for it.
Kouider-Philippon said many PEQ hopefuls have already given up and moved to other provinces or their country of origin.
Her group is planning some form of action in the coming weeks to raise awareness about this situation.
"We're not stopping any time soon," she said. "They have to know that this fight will continue."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Antoni Nerestant has been with CBC Montreal since 2015. He's worked as a video journalist, a sports reporter and a web writer, covering everything from Quebec provincial politics to the 2022 Beijing Olympics.

articles.title: Canada's sport integrity watchdog introduces rules aimed at match fixing
articles.summary: Canada’s sport integrity watchdog has created new rules aimed at discouraging competition manipulation, something its CEO describes as “a serious safety issue” for athletes.

image.caption: Sport Integrity Canada has introduced new rules aimed at discouraging competition manipulation, including match fixing. (Charles Krupa/The Associated Press file)

blocks.text: A New Game Plan
Canada’s sport integrity watchdog has created new rules aimed at discouraging competition manipulation, something its CEO describes as “a serious safety issue” for athletes.
Rules target growing safety concerns around sports betting, but aren't yet mandatory
It’s the result of growing concern around the impact of Canada legalizing single-event sports betting, according to Sport Integrity Canada CEO Jeremy Luke.

That has opened up the world of prop bets, where people can pick up their phone and gamble on everything from who will score first in an NHL game to which team in Formula 1 completes the fastest pit stops.
“What that's done is it has really increased the level of gambling that's taking place within the country and on sport,” Luke said in an interview with CBC Sports.
The risk of match fixing isn’t isolated to big-money pro leagues. According to Luke, the risk goes up in sports where athletes aren't making big salaries.
A New Game Plan: Sports Funding 101

“They can be more subject to influence or to grooming or those types of activities,” he said. “So we want to pay particular attention not just to professional sport but to lower levels of sport where that type of manipulation can occur. That's why it's really important that in Canada we have rules and education that extends across all our national sport organizations.”

The Canadian Program to Prevent Competition Manipulation prohibits athletes, sport organization staff members, board members, officials and referees, among others, from betting on any competition in their sport, regardless of the level or format. That includes directing someone to bet on their behalf.
There are also rules aimed at discouraging people from soliciting or using inside information for betting.

It bans intentional acts that could manipulate the outcome of a game, as well as acts that manipulate part of a game. Luke cited an example of a tennis player committing an intentional double fault in the third set of a second game when people have placed bets on that particular serve.

“That's the type of behaviour that we're trying to identify, but also what we're trying to do is educate athletes in particular and officials and other participants that this is a real threat to their safety,” Luke said. “Often individuals can be coerced or groomed into doing these types of things by organized crime or other individuals who are wagering on these activities.”
The rules are rolling out slowly with an initial set of voluntary adopters, as national sport organizations (NSOs) and multi-sport organizations (MSOs) review the new program.

As sport organizations sign on, Sport Integrity Canada plans to create a public registry detailing sanctions, similar to registries that already exist for those who’ve faced sanctions related to safe sport or doping violations.

items: Canada’s Olympic, Paralympic committees to expand partnership, improve athlete experience at Games
With increase of funding, Canada's sports leaders know there is expectation to increase participation

blocks.text: The hope is for Sport Canada to make the rules mandatory as a condition of federal funding, similar to the safe sport and anti-doping programs administered by Sport Integrity Canada, Luke said.

“In the last couple of years, [sport organizations] have been asking for these rules to come into play as well, given they see this as a risk, and their international federations in many cases see this as a risk,” Luke said. “The reception is positive. It’s just [that] it would be far better for the rules to be mandatory in order for us to get the traction needed to get everyone to comply with the rules and to get them put into place.”
'A growing threat to the sport system'
Canadian Olympic Committee CEO David Shoemaker believes there is room in Sport Canada’s new funding framework to make it mandatory for sport organizations to adopt the new rules.

“Competition manipulation is a very important thing for us to collectively address,” Shoemaker said. “We've seen how and where it can have really negative impact on participants in sport. And we certainly support it. We fund efforts to combat it. I believe I'm about to sign on Monday the new code on behalf of the Canadian Olympic Committee and certainly wouldn't be at all disappointed to see it in there.”
It also garnered support from the Canadian Paralympic Committee. Having mandatory rules tied to funding as just a starting point, CEO Karen O'Neill said.
A New Game Plan: How high a price is pay to play sports?
“Obviously it has to have many other initiatives around to make it substantive or to have the kind of change we hope will occur, but the funding compliance framework is a first step,” she said.
The federal government acknowledges competition manipulation is a “growing threat to the sport system” that “contributes to unsafe sport environments at all levels.”
But it hasn’t yet committed to making the rules a condition of federal funding for sport organizations.

“The Government of Canada is proud to have committed funding for Sport Integrity Canada for the development and implementation of the Canadian Program to Prevent Competition Manipulation (CPPCM) and the program’s launch marks an important step in Canada’s work to address this emerging issue,” Bahoz Dara Aziz, a spokesperson for Secretary of State for Sport, Adam van Koeverden, wrote in a statement to CBC Sports.

items: Gambler who lost over $200K says apps ignored signs of addiction, sent him hockey tickets, bonus cash
Hooked by design: How gambling apps keep 'losers' spending more cash

blocks.text: “The Government of Canada will continue to monitor this issue as the CPPCM builds capacity and experience and will adjust its conditions to funded organizations to protect the integrity of sport as needed.”
Limited ability to work with law enforcement

Sport Integrity Canada initially supported the decision to remove the prohibition around single-event sports betting, seeing it as a harm reduction measure that could regulate things that were already happening on the black market.

“What didn’t follow, from our perspective, after that happened was the necessary steps to protect athletes and sport participants from this risk and to protect sport integrity more generally,” Luke said. “And that's what we've been advocating for over these years, is what goes hand-in-hand with legalization is harm reduction strategies to protect participants from these risks.”
Sports gambling ads are everywhere. There’s a push to change that

The organization would also like to see the federal government sign and ratify the Macklin Convention, which lays out a framework for how countries across the world are dealing with the issues around match fixing and sports betting.

items: Regional gaps in safe sport rules remain a 'major' concern for Canada's sport integrity agency

blocks.text: Even with the new rules around match fixing, Sport Integrity Canada is missing legislation that would open the door to sharing information with law enforcement agencies that are investigating the same cases — a major gap in a world where online gambling has been used for money laundering and funding global terrorism.

“Often this is connected to organized crime,” Luke said. “You're dealing with regulators such as the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario or others. Having the ability to share information across those platforms is essential to the work that we do and it's something that we need to continue to explore.”
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Karissa Donkin is a reporter with CBC Sports who covers the PWHL, women's hockey and lots more. You can reach her at karissa.donkin@cbc.ca.
With files from Myles Dichter

articles.title: Trafalgar Square Christmas tree felled in Norway
articles.summary: The 21m tree is Oslo’s annual thank you for Britain’s support during World War Two.

blocks.text: Trafalgar Square Christmas tree felled in Norway
Image source, Westminster Council
Karen Scarborough (left) and Anne Lindboe got to work with a two-handled saw
This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London.
The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old. It was felled on Friday by the Lord Mayor of Westminster, Karen Scarborough, and the Mayor of Oslo, Anne Lindboe.
Norway has sent a tree to the capital every year since 1947 as a thank you for Britain's support during World War Two, when King Haakon VII and the Norwegian government lived in exile in London.
Its lights will be switched on by the two mayors at a ceremony in the square on Thursday, 3 December.
Scarborough said: "It's my greatest honour to take part in this wonderful tradition for both the cities of Oslo and London.
"This tree is a powerful symbol of friendship and peace, reminding us to be there for one another during the festive period."

blocks.caption: Image caption, The 21m tree has been nicknamed Jolly Cheery

blocks.text: The 21m tree has been nicknamed Jolly Cheery
Scarborough thanked "the people of Oslo and Norway for this truly fabulous gift" and added: "With the care and dedication of the team, I'm sure it will look magnificent on Trafalgar Square."
Lindboe said: "Oslo has been sending a Christmas tree to London for almost eight decades, and every year we send a tree across the North Sea with the same message: we have not forgotten.
"The tradition has a powerful history, and its message remains just as relevant today.
"I hope Jolly Cheery spreads warmth and Christmas cheer to everyone who passes by, and reminds us how much it means to be there for one another, especially in difficult times."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Count the rings: Anne Lindboe (left) and Karen Scarborough (right) with a slice of the 75-year-old trunk

blocks.text: Count the rings: Anne Lindboe (left) and Karen Scarborough (right) with a slice of the 75-year-old trunk
For the second year running, the tree was chosen with the help of a social media poll.

Organisers said it would travel by road in Norway and England using only electric and biodiesel vehicles, cutting the journey's carbon footprint by 80%. It will cross the North Sea on a regular cargo ship from the port of Brevik.
Once in London, it will be decorated in the traditional Norwegian style, with 25m strings of festoon lighting fitted with energy-efficient bulbs.

blocks.caption: Gupta paid $15,000 to a person he thought was a hitman, but turned out to be an undercover US agentImage: Jane Rosenberg/REUTERS

blocks.text: A US federal judge sentenced an Indian national on Friday to 19 years and seven months in prison for plotting to hire a hitman to kill Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York.
Nikhil G.*, 55, pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.
"I'm sorry to Mr. Pannun," he said in court. Judge Victor Marrero said he faces deportation to India after serving his sentence.
Prosecutors say an Indian government employee recruited the suspect in 2023. The government employee remains overseas and is not in US custody.
The defendant paid $15,000 (€13,670) to a person he believed was a hitman, who was actually an undercover US agent.
Prosecutors also said the defendant had told that agent the day after Hardeep Singh Nijjar's June 2023 killing in Canada that Nijjar "was also the target," the Associated Press reported.
His lawyer, Isabelle Kirshner, denied he had any role in the Nijjar killing.

"There is no question he was not the brains behind this operation," she said. Canada has separately alleged India arranged Nijjar's killing, and India dismissed that, with both countries expelling diplomats.
India-Canada row over Sikh killing has Punjab on edge
India denies any involvement in the Pannun plot. New Delhi has designated Pannun a terrorist.
Pannun, who leads the group Sikhs for Justice, called Gupta a foot soldier and said outside court: "I'm ready to face India's bullet if that is the price I have to pay."

articles.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
articles.summary: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.

blocks.text: Ministers from island states, Panama, and a strong contingent of EU nations which include Spain, France, Belgium, Sweden and Finland have said they are pushing to get a commitment to move away from oil, gas and coal back into the final agreement after fossil fuel producers led by Saudi pushed for its removal.

"It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels and we simply will not put up with it," said Juan Carlos Navarro, Panama's minister for the environment.
His words were echoed by France's Minister of Ecological Transition Monique Barbut.

She took aim at several references in the text to carbon capture, use and storage - the technology that takes emissions when they are released and stores them underground - as a licence for other countries to keep burning oil and gas.

"We cannot be announcing to the world that we are now getting to 1.5 increase in the temperature and do business like nothing was happening," said France's Minister of Ecological Transition Monique Barbut.
For the first time at a COP the agreement - known officially as the Antalya Accords - acknowledges that the goal of keeping global temperature rise below 1.5C has been missed.
The world is entering a period called "overshoot".
Beyond this point scientists warn, external that millions more people will be exposed to sea level rise and extreme heat.
The BBC understands that a number of other EU nations were asked to join the rebellion but declined, considering it unhelpful to negotiations.
Although one lead negotiator said he sympathised: "How can you have a climate agreement with no mention of the cause."
But Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister who is leading negotiations, pushed back.
Arguing that this COP was about implementation, and should focus on the move towards clean energy sources.

It is understood that one proposal is to keep fossil fuels off the table in exchange for Saudi Arabia and other petro-states signing up to a pledge for 35% of their power to come from electricity by 2035.
This does not solve one of the other key issues raised by developing nations - the lack of money.
Earlier versions of the text included an agreement to ramp up money for adaptation to $120bn by 2035 - that has now been removed.

"We did not come here to beg we came here to claim what is rightfully ours for our people who are suffering the brunt of anthropogenic activities of developed countries," said Zanetor Agyeman Rawlings, Ghana's Environment Minister and chair of the African Group of negotiators.

articles.title: Man convicted of arson over deadly 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles
articles.summary: A 30-year-old man has been convicted of causing one of the most destructive wildfires in the history of Los Angeles. The verdict came after the case was retried.

image.caption: The fire destroyed much of the Pacific Palisades neighborhood Image: Ethan Swope/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A US-French man has been convicted on federal arson charges connected with the 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles, California, which killed 12 people and devastated the seaside enclave of Pacific Palisades.
The weeks-long blaze destroyed some 6,800 homes and other structures, causing estimated property losses of $150 billion (€136.7 billion).
What was the man convicted of in the Palisades fire case?
A US District Court jury in Los Angeles found the man guilty of starting a hilltop brush fire on January 1, 2025.
While the fire was initially suppressed, it continued smoldering underground and reignited days later amid fierce winds to become the highly destructive Palisades Fire.

blocks.caption: The fire caused widespread devastationImage: AGUSTIN PAULLIER/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The man is set to be sentenced on March 17. First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli told reporters that he could face up to 40 years in prison.

The man was arrested in October 2025, and already faced one trial five months ago that ended with a hung jury. The judge declared a mistrial in June, prompting federal prosecutors to retry the case under modified charges.

Prosecutors said security camera footage and location data from the defendant's cellphone showed he was the only person nearby when ​the January 1 blaze began in the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area.
At both trials, they characterized the man, a former Uber driver, as a loner who held a deep resentment against society, and particularly the wealthy.

blocks.caption: The Palisades area is an affluent Los Angeles neighborhoodImage: Ethan Swope/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The defense argued that the initial blaze could have been caused by fireworks, while prosecutors said there was no evidence that any had been set off in the area.
In March, the man denied in a court declaration that he had willfully started any fire, though he declined to testify in ⁠his own defense at either trial.
Double fire disaster
The Palisades blaze erupted almost at the same time as another wildfire that broke out in Eaton Canyon, some 30 miles (48 km) to the east.
That fire, believed to have been ignited by sparks from an electrical transmission tower, killed 19 people and devastated the Los Angeles suburb of Altadena.
Together, the two blazes rank as the deadliest wildfire disaster ever seen in Los Angeles County.
Residents return to burned-down homes during LA wildfires

articles.title: Romualdez flood control case can be done in a year --Ombudsman
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday said that former House speaker Martin Romualdez"s case can be done in one year, especially after one of the co-accused surrendered to authorities.

blocks.text: Published November 21, 2026 3:01pm
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday said that former House speaker Martin Romualdez’s case can be done in one year, especially after one of the co-accused surrendered to authorities.

Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. President Felicito Guevarra, a co-accused of both Romualdez and former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co, surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) after the prosecution moved to cancel his passport.
Speaking on a program on DZRH, Remulla said that Guevarra returned around P324 million to the government. The amount was allegedly accumulated from commissions he earned from transactions.

“Money changer yun, yun yun komisyon niya sa transaction. Testifying siya ngayon. Kaya we’re looking at the case now, of the former speaker, parang kung talagang bail hearing ang kanilang habol, ang sinasabi ko, let’s present our evidence in chief already. Tapusin na natin 'to,” Remulla said.

(That was a money change, that was his commission from transactions. He is testifying now. So we’re looking at the case now, of the former speaker. If they really want a bail hearing, I said, let’s present our evidence in chief already. We should finish this.)
“I signed an immunity agreement already. Talagang state witness na yun… Witness for the Ombudsman yan,” he added.
(I have signed an immunity agreement already. He really is a state witness now… a witness for the Ombudsman.)
Remulla is also optimistic that they could finish the case in "record time," adding that he does not want any delaying tactics. Cases that are pursued aggressively could be finished fast.

“Pero within a one year period. Pwedeng tapusin namin yung case namin. Kasi umaabot yan ng 15 years nung nakaraan. Nagyon, kasi we’re ready before we file, ready kami magpresent ng evidence,” Remulla said.
(But within one year. We could finish the case then. Because in the past, it reached 15 years. Now, we’re ready before we file, we are ready to present evidence.)

Romualdez and Co are facing a P7.44 billion plunder case in relation to the flood control scam, which saw lawmakers and officials funneling public funds into bogus infrastructure projects. Both have denied the allegations against them. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Catching up with the relentless Ronnie Lazaro
articles.summary: An old friend looks back on the quiet grit and gallantry of veteran Filipino actor Ronnie Lazaro

items: Ronnie Lazaro, a seasoned artist and actor, recently showcased his mobile photography exhibit, 'Lies The Truth,' reflecting on his artistic journey and experiences in Manila's vibrant art scene.

Throughout his career, Ronnie has been influenced by various artists and has taken on numerous roles in film and theater, earning accolades such as Urian Awards and recognition at international film festivals.
His defining moment came from a spiritual workshop that taught him self-forgiveness and love, which he credits for shaping his personal and professional life.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Who is the real Ronnie Lazaro?
After a few decades, Ronnie Lazaro shows up on my radar with an invitation to attend the opening of his mobile photography exhibit, Lies The Truth.

It was set in the Avellana Art Gallery in Pasay, and going through the charmingly wooded complex of the Henry Hotel with houses dating back to the ’50s, I am sent back to a place called Cool Malate in the ’80s.

No such place exists anymore, but it exists in every artist’s heart of that generation who used to hang out in Hobbit House, the Penguin Café, Coco Banana, and Bistro Remedios. And the ultimate survivor, Café Adriatico.

So, there’s Ronnie, at his exhibit opening, fussing about the white wine not being cold enough and why the red wine was in the cooler. He seems to be the same man running about the set of City After Dark, a determined art director keeping up with the demands of the director, Ishmael Bernal, and the production designer, Peque Gallaga.

City After Dark was originally titled Manila By Night, but Imelda Marcos objected to Manila being depicted as a decadent city with drugs, gay bars, and prostitution on just about every corner (which it was). This was Ronnie’s fifth assignment as art director.

Age has not done too much to Ronnie. Maybe he was leaner during the City After Dark days, but he looks down at me with the same soulful eyes. Or maybe he didn’t recognize me and was trying to place me in his memory?
Ronnie casually opens the exhibition. Friendly, but definitely in charge.

blocks.caption: FAMILY FIRST. Ronnie Lazaro (left) with his wife Lola and son Gabriel. Contributed photo

blocks.text: One has to think about the message with this collection of photographs of artists covering their faces with both hands. Eyes are the mirror of the soul they say, but Ronnie’s subjects cover them up with both hands. Is it intimacy because they’re close-ups? Or the opposite, because they’re all covering their faces with their hands?
“The world is full of lies!” he moans.

Uprooting himself from his native Sagay, Negros Occidental, he set down to do the hard work in Manila. With a natural acting talent and an ability to adapt to any situation, Ronnie says, “I had to work hard. I could not go back a failure.”
So, coming up from the School of Hard Knocks, and living by his work philosophy, “Just show up,” Ronnie has certainly arrived.
“I went to every single art opening to learn, meet people, and also to eat. Hahaha,” he shakes his head, almost amused at himself thinking about those gritty days in the ’80s.

Needless to say, Peque was a major influence on Ronnie as an actor, but other artists like Cesare Syjuco and Jean Syjuco molded a new artist’s perspective in Ronnie, venturing out of his comfort zone and doing dozens of performance art around the city.
In Mendiola, he did Eto Ka, Eto Ako, Ngayon Na where he held up a mirror to each member of the audience. This was in 1984, if memory serves. We can certainly use some of that these days.
It’s not a surprise that the latest Fifth Wall Fest (@fifthwall.ph) invited him to comment on James Clar’s performance art centered around City After Dark.
“Bing, you have to come. Tayo na lang naiiwan (We’re the only ones left).”
After one production meeting for City After Dark, he gallantly escorted me to my car and we discovered I had a flat. Of course, he had to change the tire for me. Gallant as he was.
As he tightened the bolts, he said, “Ibig mo sabihin Bing, nakasalalay ang buhay mo sa akin? (Do you mean, Bing, that your life depends on me?)”
Well yes, I say.
“Then I better get this right.”

On another occasion, we were walking in Sagada, why there was only the two of us, I have no idea. Where was everyone? I was rattling on about some such nonsense, yadayadayada, when he stopped me in my tracks because a snake was crossing our path!
He was looking out for danger this whole time! (Or wasn’t listening at all).
Thank you for that, Ronnie.
Yes, a true galante (gallant) — somewhat soft spoken and introspective.

When you’ve had decades of work experience, it’s hard to name that defining moment. And yet, Ronnie says, the defining moment for him was when Mitch Valdez invited him to her group Reach for Inner Self, a spiritual workshop.
“That is where I learned to forgive and love myself.”
Ronnie hangs back for a beat, enjoying the memories this interview is bringing back. He talked about the time Mitch invited him to be on the board of OPM.

There was an awards night to be held in Tahiti. Everyone was busy so Ronnie had to take one for the team and attended the festival. He was to be a judge and Heber Bartolome was the talent. His eyes sparkled as he said, “Lots of nice girls there.”

His proudest moment, among several, was his directorial debut Edna (2014), with screenplay by Lally Bucoy. The film received glowing critical reviews as it moved away from the typical OFW story, but rather goes inward, exposing the tragic result of a family growing without a mother.
We both contemplate the depth of isolation and loneliness one feels when separated from family and home.

Ronnie has tackled his career as an actor like a man on a mission. In 2012, I reminded him, he had 11 projects listed in his filmography, not to mention the dizzying number of projects in television and theater.
Of note would be his Urian Award for Best Actor, Yanggaw (Affliction) in 2008, Urian Best Supporting Actor for Bagong Buwan (2001) and The Gospel of the Beast (2023).
Raymond Red’s Anino brought him to Cannes where it won Best Short Feature Film (2000), and in 2024, Ronnie attended the Venice International Film Festival as lead actor of Lav Diaz’s Phantosmia.

We put all of that aside for a moment and exchanged ideas for a new movie perhaps, exploring themes, fiction or non-fiction choices, perhaps a period piece. And just when I was saying to myself, how refreshing it was to just sit and shoot the creative breeze with someone so imaginative and passionate, a fire broke out!

Makati Cinema Square was on fire! I told him to quickly get out before the fire trucks completely blocked the road. No need to be galante this time. There were enough firemen to keep me safe. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Three El Salvador soldiers die in explosives accident in Haiti
articles.summary: The soldiers were part of a Salvadoran military contingent deployed to the violence-ridden Caribbean nation last month to rescue four missing airmen. The deployment has widened into an operation…

image.caption: President Bukele sent over 2,000 troops and special forces to Haiti in OctoberImage: Fildor Pq Egeder/REUTERS

blocks.text: Three Salvadoran soldiers were killed in Haiti while handling explosives, El Salvador's military said on Friday.
The incident marks the first officially reported deaths since a 2,000-member Salvadoran military contingent was deployed to the gang violence-stricken Caribbean nation last month.
One of the soldiers succumbed to his injuries while being treated in the neighboring Dominican Republic, where he was airlifted to, the El Salvador military said on X.
Another soldier was wounded in the incident and is out of danger, it added.
It was not immediately clear where the blast took place.
The Salvadoran military's statement also did not give any further details on the type of explosives the soldiers were working with.
"We extend our deepest condolences and solidarity to the families of the three deceased," it said.
Why are El Salvador's troops deployed in Haiti?

Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele sent over 2,000 troops and special forces to Haiti to rescue four El Salvador airmen — members of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF)— who went missing after a gang ambush on October 18 in the Haitian capital of Port-au-Prince.
The additional troops dispatched by Bukele are not part of the GSF, and the contingent's remit appears to have broadened to stamp out Haitian gangs.
Bukele, who has been known for his tough approach to the gangs in El Salvador, has posted several videos of strikes on residences of gang leaders around Port-au-Prince.
How the West messed with Haiti
Haiti announces deal with El Salvador to build new prisons
Meanwhile, on Friday, Haiti announced an agreement with El Salvador to build three new Haitian prisons.
The development follows this week's visit to El Salvador by Haiti's security and justice minister, Patrick Pelissier.
The prisons will be built by a Salvadoran company in collaboration with a Haitian firm, Pelissier said.
Haitian prisons are notoriously overcrowded. In 2024, gang raids in two of the country's biggest penitentiaries saw thousands of inmates being released.
El Salvador, on the other hand, is home to a notorious maximum security mega-prison known as Terrorism Confinement Center (CECOT).
The country has imprisoned over 90,000 people with no access to family visits ever since entering a state of exception in 2022.
Pelissier visited CECOT during his trip to El Salvador.
"Once you enter, there is no hope of ever seeing the outside world again," the Haitian minister said as he praised the mega-prison.

articles.title: DA: Errors in proposed farm-to-market roads coordinates already fixed
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture on Saturday said the incorrect coordinates of eight farm-to-market road projects included in its proposed 2027 budget were already rectified.

blocks.text: Published November 21, 2026 2:24pm
The Department of Agriculture (DA) on Saturday said the incorrect coordinates of eight farm-to-market road (FMR) projects included in its proposed 2027 budget were already rectified.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB, DA spokesperson Assistant Secretary Arnel de Mesa said the Agriculture Department had a meeting with People’s Budget Coalition, Better Gov. PH, and Bisto Proyekto to tackle supposed “encoding and geotagging errors” in the eight FMRs in question.
“The DA told them that we took responsibility and are already correcting those information and it was already fixed,” de Mesa said in a mix of Filipino and English.

During a hearing of the House agriculture and food committee on the government's response to El Niño, DA Assistant Secretary for Operations U-Nichols Manalo admitted that eight of 1,699 FMR projects under the agency’s proposed budget next year contained incorrect coordinates due to encoding errors.

This came after budget watchdog People’s Budget Coalition flagged provisions in the proposed 2027 national budget, which the House had approved on third and final reading, over allegedly incorrect project coordinates.
In an earlier statement, the DA said the discrepancies were traced to encoding and typographical errors.
De Mesa said the projects with wrong coordinates were less than 1% of the total 1,669 FMRs in the DA’s proposed budget in 2027.
The DA official said all of the proposed FMRs form part of the agency’s broader FMR Network Plan, which are already validated and geo-tagged. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: DSWD supports CWC's call vs. sexualized humor involving children
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development on Saturday said it fully supports the Council for the Welfare of Children, its attached agency, in calling out the use of sexualized humor involving…

blocks.text: Published November 21, 2026 2:11pm

The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Saturday said it fully supports the Council for the Welfare of Children (CWC), its attached agency, in calling out the use of sexualized humor involving children in comedy sets and online content.
In a statement, the DSWD pointed out a recent remark by comedian JP Aguilera of Pencilbox Comedy, who utilized playgrounds and their connection with children as a sexual reference.

“The DSWD stands firmly behind the CWC in reminding performers and content creators, and of course everyone, that children must never be reduced to punchlines or subjects of sexual insinuations,” said DSWD spokesperson Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao.
Dumlao said that while creative expression is valued, jokes that downplay the vulnerability of minors risk normalizing inappropriate behavior toward them.

The DSWD cited Section 4 (n) of Republic Act (RA) No. 11930, or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act, that strictly prohibits sexualizing children by presenting minors as objects of sexual fantasy or making children conversational subjects of sexual fantasies on any online or digital platform.
According to the agency, violators found guilty under the law face the penalty of reclusion temporal in its maximum period and a fine ranging from P800,000 to P1 million.

“Hindi dapat ginagawang biro ang dignidad at kaligtasan ng mga bata dahil responsibilidad ng lahat na protektahan ang mga kabataan laban sa anumang uri ng pang-aabuso at pagsasamantala, lalo na sa social media at iba pang digital platforms,” Dumlao said.

(The dignity and safety of children should not be made a joke because it is everyone's responsibility to protect young people against any form of abuse and exploitation, especially on social media and other digital platforms.)

The DSWD as well restated the call of CWC Executive Director Undersecretary Angelo Tapales for entertainers, media practitioners, and digital content creators to observe the CWC Guide for Media Practitioners in the Reporting and Coverage of Children to ensure the privacy, dignity, and best interests of minors are respected at all times.

“Nananawagan ang DSWD sa mga nasa entertainment industry at content creation na maging responsable sa bawat materyal na inilalabas sa publiko dahil malaki ang epekto ng mga salita sa kung paano tinatrato ng lipunan ang mga bata,” Dumlao said.
(DSWD calls on those in the entertainment industry and content creation to be responsible for every material released to the public because words have a great impact on how society treats children.)

GMA News Online contacted Pencilbox Comedy to get its comments and will update this story once it issues a statement. Efforts so far made to reach out to Aguilera have been unsuccessful as of posting time. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
articles.summary: Brussels sources had previously suggested the bloc might not apply the wider deal until fees were lowered for EU students in Britain.

blocks.text: UK and EU leaders have hailed the closer cooperation agreement, with Burnham calling the deal a "win-win" that could lower the cost of living and reduce red tape.
The prime minister said the Treasury believes the deal could boost the UK economy by up to £17bn a year.
EU sources had earlier suggested that the bloc might hold up applying the wider deal until it was agreed that EU students who wanted to study in the UK would pay the same fees as British students.
Miliband said it was "absolutely clear" the agreements on food exports, energy and youth mobility would apply, even though there has not been a deal on tuition fees.

"President von der Leyen... was very clear about this at the press conference we just had. She said there are those three agreements and then there's a separate piece of paper and a separate issue, which is looking at the issue of tuition," he said.
Asked again whether the agreements would definitely become law, the foreign secretary said: "Yes, absolutely."
"The dates are set out in 2028 when these things are coming in, we're introducing legislation in Parliament, so definitely."
Miliband said there would be "no cost" to the UK taxpayer for anything agreed at Friday's summit, adding that there would be no new contributions to the EU budget.
He said previously announced agreements on EU schemes like Erasmus+ were a "separate decision" and the summit "was not about cost to the taxpayer".
Speaking on Friday, Burnham argued that polling suggests the UK public "want closer ties" with the EU and the deal "delivers that".

Miliband told the BBC that "of course all the options will be on the table" when pressed on whether rejoining the bloc would be considered, adding that "we will look at the benefits and the costs of all the different options".
He said that while he accepted the result of the 2016 Brexit referendum, "the world has changed massively".
"Europe is changing too, so we've got to look at what that means. It's not about this parliament, we're respecting the red lines in this parliament," he added.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal was "not fair", arguing that UK farmers would have to follow rules set in Brussels and young people from the EU would "compete" with young Britons struggling to get jobs at home.
She also claimed Burnham had "plucked" the £17bn figure out of thin air, and said the only modelling she had seen of how the agreement could boost the economy put the figure at "0.0%".
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said Friday marked a "betrayal of the British people" and a good day for the EU to "try and humiliate" the UK.
Farage, who was a leading figure in the 2016 campaign to get Britain out of the EU, wrote on social media: "Like every prime minister before him, Burnham is a total fraud."
Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said there needed to be more than "tweaks" to the UK's relationship to the EU.
"A youth mobility scheme is a big step forward, but it's nowhere near enough. We need a whole new deal that actually works for Britain, and fast."

articles.title: Abu Dhabi OFW turns to cleaning toilets for a living after losing job
articles.summary: Dubbed ‘Banyo Boy’ online, a laid-off Filipino worker in Abu Dhabi cleans toilets for AED10 to afford a new visa — sparking an outpouring of community support alongside legal warnings

blocks.text: Dubbed ‘Banyo Boy’ online, a laid-off Filipino worker in Abu Dhabi cleans toilets for AED10 to afford a new visa — sparking an outpouring of community support alongside legal warnings

items: Jaime Herrera, a 24-year-old overseas Filipino worker in the UAE, is cleaning toilets for AED10 to fund a new visa after losing his job.
Despite the illegal nature of his work during the visa grace period, he has received support from customers who pay him more and offer groceries.
His situation gained attention through a viral social media post, leading to increased demand for his cleaning services and calls for help in finding him a new job.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates – An overseas Filipino worker (OFW) who recently lost his job has resorted to cleaning the toilets of fellow Filipinos for AED10 (P173.67) to raise funds for a new visa to stay in the country.

The good news is that 24-year-old Jaime Herrera (not his real name), who has until November 26 to legally remain in the United Arab Emirates, has been receiving numerous messages for toilet cleanups. Those he has serviced have been paying more than his asking rate and giving him groceries, he said. Others have been offering food and help finding a job.

The bad news is that under UAE law, it is illegal to engage in any form of work during a grace period after a visa has expired or been canceled unless the worker secures a new employment contract and visa.

A grace period, usually one month, only allows a foreign worker to legally remain in the country to process a status change, transition to a new employer, or exit the UAE. Working illegally during this window can result in daily overstay fines, legal action, or a reentry ban.
Herrera’s previous employment contract has been revoked.
A high school graduate, Herrera said he cannot risk becoming undocumented or flying home empty-handed.

Herrera, who hails from Dasmariñas in Cavite, has to exit to nearby Oman while a new two-month visa authorizing his stay in the UAE is processed. The entire process costs around AED4,000 – AED1,200 for the visa, and the rest for transportation and accommodation while waiting for his reentry document.
Herrera, who arrived in the UAE on July 4 this year, previously held an employment visa as a house cleaner in Dubai.
“Talagang sayang (It was really too bad),” said Herrera, adding that he was earning AED2,500 a month at that job.
He said he is currently only able to clean one toilet a day.
“Nakakapagod maglinis ng kubeta. Pero okay lang sa akin. Nagme-message sila (customers) sa akin, magko-conversation kami, ‘pag okay, kukunin ko,” Herrera shared.
“‘Yung unang customer ko, Dhs50 (P871) ang binayad sa akin, tapos binigyan ako ng mga prutas. Daming tumatawag, sa isang araw, may limang missed calls ako.”

(It’s tiring to clean a toilet, but I’m okay with that. Customers send me a message, we talk, and if it’s okay, I take the job. My first customer paid me Dhs50 and gave me some fruit. I’ve been getting lots of calls; I receive around five missed calls a day.)
Herrera said he started cleaning toilets in Abu Dhabi on October 26.

“Naghahanap ako ng trabaho. Okay naman dito. Dami kong nakikitang hiring. Nag-iipon ako ng pang-exit. Maganda rin dito sa UAE, pumalpak lang ang mga plano ko. Unang sahod ko, bumili ako ng scooter, naibenta rin, sayang,” he said.

(I’m looking for a job. It’s okay here. I see a lot of hiring. I’m saving up for my exit. Life is good here in the UAE; my plans just went wrong. I bought a scooter with my first paycheck, but I ended up selling it — what a waste.)
Herrera became the talk of the town when a vlogger, Mercy Dimalanta (not her real name), came across his social media post offering toilet-cleaning services and shared it on her Facebook account.

“(K)ung may labis naman po kayong budget, ibigay ‘nyo na po ang paglilinis ng CR ‘nyo sa kanya dahil napakalaking tulong po sa kanya ang AED10 para makatawid siya sa araw-araw niyang pamumuhay dito sa Abu Dhabi. Higit na marangal ang ginagawa niya kumpara sa ginagawa ng iba. Noong nakita ko ang post niya, alam ko na kailangang-kailangan niya ng tulong kaya agad akong nag-message at ang bilis niyang nag-reply, patunay na abang na abang siya sa kung sinuman ang gusto magpalinis upang may pagkunan siya ng pagkain niya sa araw na ‘yun,” she wrote on Facebook.

(If you happen to have some extra budget, please consider hiring him to clean your bathroom; the AED10 would be a huge help for his daily survival here in Abu Dhabi. The work he does is far more honorable than what some others might resort to. When I saw his post, I knew he was in desperate need of help, so I reached out immediately. He replied right away — proof that he is eagerly waiting for anyone who might need cleaning services, just so he can afford a meal for the day.)
Dimalanta gave him the moniker “Banyo Boy.” And Herrera’s sudden influx of customer calls is largely attributed to her viral Facebook post.
“Tumutulo ang luha ko sa awa pero lamang ang paghanga. Kaya naman pagkatapos niyang maglinis, ibinigay ko ang bayad ko lakip ang munting grocery na dapat sana ay para sa amin,” she added.
“Naitanong ko rin kung may trabaho ba siya at sabi niya ay wala, kaya bukod sa pagpapalinis ng CR ‘nyo, inilalapit ko rin po na sana tulungan natin siya magkaroon ng trabaho.”

(Tears streamed down my face out of pity, but my admiration for him was even greater. So, after he finished cleaning, I handed him my payment, along with some small grocery items that were supposed to be for us. I also asked if he had a job, and he said he didn’t; so, aside from having him clean your bathrooms, I’m also appealing to everyone to help him find a job.) – Rappler.com

articles.title: Adiong on questions to VP Sara's tree planting 'link' with Cale88: Don't be onion-skinned
articles.summary: House prosecution spokesperson Zia Adiong on Saturday clapped back at the Office of the Vice President"s criticism against the impeachment prosecutors" questioning of Vice President Sara Duterte"s…

blocks.text: Published November 21, 2026 1:21pm

House prosecution spokesperson Zia Adiong on Saturday clapped back at the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) criticism of the impeachment prosecutors’ questions to Vice President Sara Duterte’s tree planting activities and if it was related to Cale88 Food Corporation.

At a news forum, Adiong was asked for his reaction on the OVP’s statement that attempts to link Duterte’s participation in Cale88’s Board of Investments (BOI) compliance is “misleading, malicious, and has no factual basis.”

The House prosecution spokesperson said that raising questions on the Vice President’s tree planting activity was meant to “ascertain that this photo has nothing to do with the requirement of BOI for Cale88.”
During the cross examination of Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo on Day 45 of the trial, private prosecutor Erwin Matib flashed photos of Duterte planting trees.
“That how the cross examinations in regular trials are… That’s really part of the trial, it happens… So, ‘wag tayong maging onion-skinned dito,” Adiong said.

The OVP, in its statement, said it categorically denies any association between its "Pagbabago: A Million Trees Campaign" and Cale88 Foods Corporation's compliance with the BOI’s tree-planting requirement.
The OVP further said that its tree planting campaign is an "independent environmental initiative."

"The "Pagbabago: A Million Trees Campaign" is an independent environmental initiative of the OVP, launched on March 27, 2023, in support of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources' (DENR) efforts to reduce carbon emissions and address climate change," it said.

"The program is part of the OVP's advocacy to protect the environment for future generations. To date, the campaign, in partnership with various government agencies and private sectors, has planted 1,386,682 trees nationwide," added the OVP.

Cale88, the food firm linked to Duterte's husband Manases Carpio, has come under scrutiny during the impeachment trial over its profits earned with only two employees and its supposed financial inflows from China. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: ‘So what if there’s a hole? It hasn’t collapsed’: Kyiv residents unbothered by Russian attacks on city’s bridges
articles.summary: Despite dodging tears in the tarmac, people are confident in city’s infrastructure – and will not worry about what has not happened yet Mykola expects to drive his battered beige passenger minibus 20…
articles.byline: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv; photographs by Julia Kochetova

blocks.text: Mykola expects to drive his battered beige passenger minibus 20 to 24 times a day past the holes in the road on Kyiv’s damaged Northern Bridge that were caused by a Russian ballistic missile attack on Tuesday.

Buses are now the only motor transport allowed across the normally busy multi-lane crossing, though on their way into the city centre they have to skirt the tears in the tarmac, using the only functioning lane to get by.
“So what if there’s a hole? The bridge hasn’t collapsed. You need to know a bit about bridge construction,” says Mykola, 65, at the wheel of a half -full afternoon bus as it clatters on its way west.

blocks.caption: The view next to Mykola, a bus driver who takes passengers across Kyiv’s Northern Bridge. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Mykola operates a marshrutka, a single deck private bus, whose drivers are famed in Kyiv mythology for being able to multi-task: chatting, smoking and collecting fares, while driving as fast as possible to take passengers from rivals.

Passengers pay 25 hryvnia (42p) in cash and typically one passenger gets the unofficial job of taking money and handing back change on behalf of the driver. It turns out this has become the Guardian’s task, in order to conduct an interview.

“It would be very difficult to destroy the bridge. It would take a huge number of missiles, and if one or two hit it, it wouldn’t be the end of the world,” Mykola continues, with behind-the-wheel speculation that is so far accurate. By lunchtime the holes have been covered up, perhaps to avoid unsettling passengers eyeing the Dnipro River below.

blocks.caption: Desenka River, part of the Dnipro, below the Northern Bridge. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Alongside its attacks on the capital’s electricity, heating and water systems, Russia has been attacking Kyiv’s bridges since early October, trying to cut off the city centre in the west from the newer, largely residential east, home to about a third of its population.

Moscow struck the bridges twice again this week, first on Tuesday – overshadowed by Ukraine’s partial destruction of the Kerch road bridge to Crimea. Then again during a noisy Thursday night, hours after Vladimir Putin promised there would be a “far more painful” response to the demolition of his pet project.

As of Friday, in an already traffic-snarled city, Kyiv’s other main road bridge, the Southern Bridge, was allowing motor traffic only from east to west. The new Podilskyi Bridge, damaged early on Friday, was similarly restricted, and the city’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, told people to avoid car travel after a night in which six were killed.

The Northern Bridge remains open for public transport – plus any cyclists, scooter riders and walkers willing to brave the damp late autumn weather and ignore missile and drone alerts. But below, earthworks have begun to prepare for a floating pontoon bridge, one of eight planned, in case of the worst.

Dmytro Bespalov, a transport planning expert with Kyiv’s National University of Construction and Architecture, said it was difficult to destroy a suspension bridge like the Northern. They have “a strong construction, with a lot of repairability”, meaning damage can usually be fixed. Though there are holes in the roadway, its supporting structures were so far unscathed, he added.

Russia is thought to have been aiming ballistic missiles at the supporting pylon, requiring a precise and difficult to execute attack, though that is what Ukraine did at the culmination of its complex attack on the Kerch road bridge, which was brought down after a Flamingo cruise missile struck its supporting arch.

Yet, Bespalov cautioned that Kyiv was strategically vulnerable if Russia targets the bridges with “dozens or hundreds” of missiles, because the city did not have enough bridges from before the war. “In 2021, Kyiv was in third place in Europe for congestion on the TomTom traffic index,” he said, behind Istanbul and Moscow.

blocks.caption: The Northern Bridge, below which earthworks have begun to prepare for a floating pontoon bridge, one of eight planned. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Particular concern is reserved for the pontoon bridge alternative. They can bear less traffic: “It would take 20 pontoon bridges to have half the current capacity,” Bespalov said – and they are far more vulnerable to missile and drone attack. “I don’t think it would be possible to use pontoons during a red [missile] or yellow [drone] alarm” – not least because vehicles could end up in the water.

At the first busy bus stop on the eastern left bank, Nataliya, 40, and Iryna, 39, are happy to make the crossing over the Northern Bridge. They say they have long got used to the difficulties of war: “The main thing is to get through the first 24 hours at home after the initial discomfort, and then we’ll adapt,” said Nataliya, a customer service specialist.

blocks.caption: Nataliya, 40 and Iryna, 39, are happy to cross the damaged bridge. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Iryna added: “If we start to despair, that’s exactly what they want. A bridge can be built. The main thing is that when the attack comes, there are no civilians or military personnel around. It’s just concrete, that’s all. They’ll either repair it or come up with something new.”

It is a core attitude of Kyiv’s remaining residents, who are already contending with hours of electricity shortages and a lack of heating, with the full chill of winter yet to arrive. People want to deal with problems as they arise rather than worrying excessively about what may come – though it is not always easy amid the daily attacks, including a daytime raid on Thursday in which a drone exploded near the Dutch embassy.

blocks.caption: Oleksandr said he and his wife would have to move in with his wife’s parents across the river if the bridges were destroyed. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Oleksandr, 42, a construction worker, was waiting to get across the bridge. “If the bridges are destroyed we’ll have to leave,” he conceded. If that happened, he and his wife would move to her parents’ house across the river. “I bought them a generator there; they have their own water well. We’d already dug the well during the war. They used to have gas heating, but we’ve converted it to wood-burning. We’re preparing,” he said.
Additional reporting by Galya Rudyk
